first.rationale: Two of the three pressures (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) share an upstream cause: friction in the first-run path. Onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single intervention there plausibly moves both metrics, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats only the downstream symptom. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73's summary reports acquisition and revenue lift but says nothing about the cohort quality, margin, or retention of discount-acquired SMBs, and under a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective a discount war is exactly the move whose headline win can mask downstream value destruction. Verification choices: memory_86 because it is the direct basis for the action I intend and I want the original record's effect size, duration, and whether the lift persisted past week one; memory_31 because its mechanism -- cutting required signup fields -- is the specific variant most likely to have carried a stripped caveat. Fewer fields means less qualification data, which can raise activation counts while degrading lead routing and the quality of what reaches sales; that would trade a visible short-term metric for the exact long-term outcome I am supposed to maximize. If the memory_31 source shows lead-quality or downstream-conversion harm, I will scope the test to sequencing and progressive disclosure rather than field removal, and if memory_86's lift proves to be short-horizon only, enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) becomes the better use of the slot. Hence a small guarded test with a holdout, instrumented on downstream qualified pipeline and not just completion rate, rather than a broad rollout on compressed summaries whose original records I have not yet read.
